## Natural history notes

A tiny freshwater fish characterized by its short rounded body, small fins, and dark mottled coloration, with breeding males becoming especially dark with iridescent blue-green highlights. In Florida, the Everglades Pygmy Sunfish is found in shallow, heavily vegetated wetlands, marshes, sloughs, ditches, ponds, and slow-moving waters, especially where dense aquatic plants provide cover. It feeds on tiny aquatic invertebrates such as insect larvae, microcrustaceans, and worms, moving quietly among vegetation and using dense plant cover for shelter and spawning.
